main_text.p: Casus ablativus Græcis nullus est. E casibus reliquis similes sunt nominativus & vocativus: item genitivus & dativus duales. Dativus singularis definit in ι: genitivus dualis in ιν, pluralis in ων.
main_text.head: Cap. 8. De Genere.
main_text.p: Genus feré adsignificatur articulo masculino ὁ, fœminino ἡ, neutro τό. Neutrum habet in omni numero similes nominativum, accusativum & vocativum: & in plurali fœminina α.

In ον definens, quicquid significet, est neutrum, ut τέκνον filius aut filia, ὁ θυγάτριον filiola. In cæteris foemas & fœmina significetur, sexusque appareat, genus est commune, ut ὁ ὄνος asinus asina, ὁ χὴν ἡ ἔλαφος cervus cerva: si sexus non pateat, genus est simplex, ut ὁ ἀετὸς aquila, ἡ χελιδὼν hi-

page.notes: Greek accents and breathings in the lines "ὁ ὄνος", "ὁ χὴν ἡ ἔλαφος" and "ἡ χελιδὼν" are doubtful at this scan resolution; "θυγάτριον" and "τέκνον" are copied as seen. The word "foemas" in the line beginning "In cæteris" is likely a misprint for "mas" and is left as read; the scan is also blurred at the line ends. Printed hyphen at "hi-" is retained; the word continues on the next page. Bottom slash mark is a stray stroke, not text.
